author: HAI
releaseNotes:
HAI Engine (Preview) 0.5.116: a rule engine for Hubitat, an alternative to Rule Machine, with a rule editor in your browser.

What's new in 0.5.116 (since 0.5.104):

* Migration page redesigned: it now says Clone throughout; the panels follow one order; a single bar at the bottom acts on the rules you tick in any panel; an arrow under the steps reverts a rule; rules that may restart the hub get their own panel with a warning; and rules a retry would not fix stay under Requires some manual intervention, with the reason.
* LIFX bulbs: the renamed applyDefault command is used when a rule is cloned (it was applyDefaultColorTemperature).
* Rules that control other rules (pause, run, private boolean) act on the HAI clone once that rule has been switched over, and the warning names any calling rule still in Rule Machine.
* Rule editor: Activate on hub for a new rule and Update on hub for one already there; Run rule runs a stopped or paused rule once without starting it; Run this step runs one line once, now; deleting several rules and drafts runs as a job on the hub with progress and a Stop button, and carries on if you close the page; Select all; one Change state menu per hub rule.
* HAI Engine page: a rewritten overview, and a banner when an update is available.
* HAI Engine is split in two: the checking and simulating now runs in HAI Checker, a hidden child app HAI adds itself, which keeps the Engine well under the hub's size limit. Package Manager installs it with the rest.
* The Toolkit opens from the hub's File Manager (hai-toolkit.html), and a help page (hai-help.html) is added. Both are installed with the other files.
* Also: Rule Machine rules are named rather than numbered in copies and the editor; Open Migration in the editor opens the Migration page itself; faster deletes of HAI copies; and security fixes for rule-to-rule calls and the stored API key.

This is a preview for invited testers. Expect rough edges, and keep your Rule Machine rules until you trust the HAI copies.

An install or update takes 10 to 15 minutes while the hub compiles the apps. Leave the page open until it finishes; your rules keep running.

* Rule editor: open it from the HAI Engine page. Build rules from triggers, conditions and actions in everyday words, check them, put them on the hub stopped, and start them when ready. Start from a pattern, or open the Showcase rule to see much of what HAI can do.
* AI Rule Assistant (optional): describe a rule in plain words and it drafts one for you to review. It needs your own Claude API key and a spending limit, under AI token and cost management. Everything else works without it.
* Each rule runs as its own small app on the hub, with its run history.
* Backups: a backup of your rules every night, and Back up now at any time. Restore one rule or all.
* HAI Migration (installed, off until you turn it on in HAI Engine): copies Rule Machine rules into HAI one at a time. One page: Assess sorts your rules into can clone, can't clone and empty; Clone makes paused copies; Cut over pauses the Rule Machine rule and starts its copy; Rollback reverses it. Needs Automation Map 2.4.48 or later, with a scan done.
* Off until you switch them on: the MCP endpoint for AI assistants, and the web address for dashboards and shortcuts.

After installing: Apps, Add user app, HAI Engine (Preview). Open the rule editor from its page, check Approved devices, and press Done.

Report a problem or give feedback: More, Report a problem or give feedback in the editor, or the Issues tab of the HAI-Engine repository on GitHub. Report security problems privately, as SECURITY.md explains.
